_note: The Story of Prophet Ayyub (Job), a descendant of Ibrahim through Ishaq, drawn strictly from the Qur'an (Surahs al-Anbiya, Sad, an-Nisa, al-An'am). The prophet of patience through affliction. Verse text resolves from the loaded Qur'an. No figural imagery; summaries carry no Arabic script.

events.title: The Affliction
events.summary: Remember Our servant Ayyub, when he called to his Lord, 'Satan has touched me with hardship and torment.' A man once given wealth, family, and health lost them all and was worn down by long sickness — yet he turned not away from his Lord.
events.why: The Qur'an frames the deepest suffering as a trial, not a punishment. Ayyub, stripped of everything, becomes the very emblem of the believer whose faith is tested to its limit.

events.title: The Prayer of the Patient
events.summary: Ayyub called upon his Lord: 'Indeed adversity has touched me, and You are the most merciful of the merciful.' He never complained against Allah, only laid his need before Him. And Allah said, 'Indeed We found him patient — an excellent servant. He was ever turning back to Us.'
events.why: His prayer is the model of complaint that is not complaint: he names his pain to Allah alone, and appeals only to His mercy. The Qur'an crowns it with the highest praise — 'an excellent servant.'
events.locator2: Book of the Prophets, no. 3391 — Ayyūb and the gold locusts: 'I cannot do without Your blessing'

events.title: Strike with Your Foot
events.summary: It was said to him, 'Strike with your foot; this is a spring, cool and refreshing to bathe in and to drink.' So a spring gushed up at his foot, and by it Allah removed his affliction and restored his health — mercy answering patience at last.
events.why: The cure comes by a simple command and a spring from the ground — a reminder that healing, like affliction, is wholly in Allah's hand, and arrives in His time for those who wait upon Him.

events.title: Family Restored and Doubled
events.summary: We removed what afflicted him and gave him back his family, and the like of them with them — a mercy from Us and a reminder for the worshippers. And that he might keep an oath he had sworn without harshness, he was told, 'Take in your hand a bundle of grass and strike with it, and do not break your oath.' — a gentle way out for a gentle servant.
events.why: Patience is rewarded not only with restoration but with abundance, and even Ayyub's oath is honoured by the softest possible means. The Qur'an holds his whole story up as 'a reminder for the worshippers.'

paths.title: The Arc of Ayyub
paths.blurb: The trial that stripped away everything, the prayer that never complained, the healing spring, and the family restored and doubled.
